intent: Split steam_compatibility.sh (663 lines) into an entry script and four sourced libraries, all under the 250-line cap, moving every function verbatim.
changes: Grouped by what each function touches rather than by size: requirement parsing and scoring with the hardware detection that feeds it, the Steam/ProtonDB API calls, credential and presentation helpers, and the run loop with the cache it reads.

The grouping was driven by the SC2034 writer/reader rule rather than chosen freely. Two arrangements were discarded first: detect_system alone in a lib writes SYSTEM_CPU_CLASS, SYSTEM_GPU_VENDOR and SYSTEM_RAM_GB without reading them, and load_cache_map alone writes CACHE_MAP without reading it. Both were fixed by moving the writer next to its reader - detect_system beside score_game, load_cache_map beside main.
The entry script is now colours, defaults, the four source lines, parse_args, the tiny log/die/vlog helpers, and `main "$@"`.

verification.evidence: IDENTICAL: all 33 top-level functions moved verbatim, re-checked after each regrouping.
Prints the full usage block and exits 0. This is a real run of the split script: it proves all four source lines resolve and that main dispatches, which no static check can show.

verification.command: shellcheck on each of the four libraries standalone
verification.evidence: All clean, with no suppression added. The pre-commit hook runs shellcheck without -x, so each file has to stand on its own.

verification.command: Sourcing each library in a subshell
verification.evidence: All four source with no side effects.
25 files over cap, down from 26. The five files are 140, 199, 156, 124 and 103 lines.

risks: --help exits before any network call, so the run exercises argument parsing and the source graph but not the API paths. Those need Steam credentials and a network round-trip, which is not something to trigger from a split verification.
Four libraries is more indirection than three would be, but the writer/reader rule fixed the grouping: merging any two would either put a writer away from its reader or push a file back over the cap.
rollback: git revert the commit; the entry script returns to 663 lines and the four libraries disappear.
After rollback, confirm steam_compatibility.sh --help still prints usage and exits 0.
